entries.title: Isaiah 58:1
segments: God's ambassadors must not spare the sins of his people, whatever be the rank and standing of the transgressors, but must rebuke them with all plainness and fidelty.

entries.title: Isaiah 58:2
segments: Great exactness and scrupulousness in respect to the outward observances of religion is often connected with great wickedness of heart and life.

entries.title: Isaiah 58:3
segments: Afflicted our soul; by such mortifications as are mentioned

. 
 
  Find pleasure; indulge your lusts. 
 
  Your labors; the oppressive services which you impose upon your dependents.  This is the way of all Pharisees, who "disfigure their faces, that they may appear unto men to fast," and at the same time "devour widows' houses," and practise "extortion and excess."

When men complain that their services are not noticed and rewarded by God, they show clearly that their supposed services are an abomination in his sight, the fruit of formality and self-righteousness.

entries.title: Isaiah 58:4
segments: For strife and debate; their fasting was a cloak for strife and debate.  Compare

. 
 
  On high; in heaven.  Such fasting as this will not gain for you acceptance with God. 
 
vv 4-7. 
 
The true spirit of fasting lies in inward sorrow for sin, and hearty renunciation of it in every form.  Outward mortifications are of no value, except as they express the inward humiliation of the soul before God.  When men cleave to their wicked practices, and seek to cover them under the cloak of outward rites and penances, they provoke the wrath of Him who cannot be deceived and will not be mocked.

entries.title: Isaiah 58:7
segments: From thine own flesh; thy brethren.
But this must be understood of all who need our help.  Compare our Lord's answer to the question, "Who is my neighbor?"

entries.title: Isaiah 58:8
segments:
Thy righteousness shall go before thee; before Israel, to remove all obstacles from his path.  The reference is to the journey from Egypt to the land of Canaan. 
 
  The glory of the Lord; an allusion to the pillar of cloud and fire, which went behind the Israelites in their passage through the Red sea, and protected them from Pharaoh and his host.

vv 8-12. 
 
When God's people truly repent of their sins, and bring forth fruits meet for repentance, he does not delay to hear their prayers, and bless them with his presence and salvation.

entries.title: Isaiah 58:9
segments: The putting forth of the finger; a sign of scorn, like making a wide mouth, and drawing out the tongue.

entries.title: Isaiah 58:10
segments: Draw out thy soul; let thy compassion go forth in deeds of love.

entries.title: Isaiah 58:13
segments:
From the sabbath; from trespassing upon its sanctity. 
 
  The holy of the Lord, honorable; that is, call the holy day of the Lord an honorable day. 
 
vv 13-14. 
 
God has appointed the Sabbath as a day of holy rest, not only from worldly labor, but also from worldly thoughts and conversation.  They only call it "a delight" and "honorable" who, with glad and willing hearts, devote it sacred hours to communion with God and spiritual labors for the good of their fellow men; and all such receive an abundant reward in the light of God's countenance and the rich communications of his grace.

entries.title: Isaiah 58:14
segments: Ride upon the high places of the earth; have victory and dominion over thine enemies.
